reading: Full proposal and all six reports. Checked pooled IGCIP effects and age-specific task administration in DeFreese2024; other citations selectively assessed, not exhaustively verified.

A.rationale: The analysis of the mismatch between indirect effect power, annual developmental indicators, and dense auditory measurements is insightful, and line 42 correctly understands that alternative mechanisms are the research motivation. However, line 70 claims that even tentative causal hypothesis goals cannot be achieved, and line 9 rejects the study because it can only explore, failing to respect the estimation-oriented positioning already adopted in the application. Line 34 adds overlapping comorbidity and cognitive exclusion proportions to assert that only 30–40% are eligible, and line 88 uses this to give a screening number of 180–240 and arbitrarily adds a fourth year of recruitment. Line 74 changes the active reduction of tasks for younger children due to time/attention burden into an inability to complete them, then speculates about floor effects, distorting the meaning of the literature.

B.rationale: Useful distinctions are made regarding power, missingness, and feasibility, and line 77 correctly points out that bootstrap cannot fix informative missingness. However, line 69 calls the standard care after joint optimization and stabilization in both arms 'control contamination,' line 71 incorrectly states that the waiting group only generates a program at 12 months, and line 162 further asserts that switching to an equivalence/non-inferiority framework would not require a larger sample, ignoring margins and precision requirements. Line 87 says the annual target totals about 72, whereas the actual table shows 56–64; these reduce the reliability of the suggestions.

C.rationale: There are practical power and missingness issues, but the core objection rewrites the application: lines 32–48 simplify a project that explicitly studies alternative temporal/language pathways into a mandatory spectral resolution chain, then treat non-significant cross-sectional results as evidence that this chain has been broken. Line 56 asserts without basis that the waiting group knows their assignment, conflicting with the planned double-blinding and identical procedures, and imports biases from psychotherapy waiting-list designs. Line 60's claim that a significant intervention effect with random assignment automatically makes it a valid instrumental variable for mediation is also unfounded. The rejection is primarily based on overly strong inferences.

D.rationale: The main scientific objectives are read fairly accurately, without inheriting the view that 'the spectral pathway has been disproven so it is not worth doing.' The shortcoming lies in elevating numerous unelaborated operational details—training, version control, home testing procedures—into grounds for rejection, while overlooking the MNAR analysis issues that the application itself clearly exposes. Lines 55/163 demand an unspecified minimum number of electrodes, but line 98 already specifies more than eight; line 53 writes auditory measurements as 7–9 times when it is actually seven, and line 73 confuses two types of dropout.

E.rationale: It provides the most complete explanation of the stratified scientific value, does not equate average null effects with the entire project being worthless, and correctly reads the annual measurements and N60 precision. However, line 84 calls MNAR without imputation plus bootstrap 'conservative and reasonable,' and describes dropout without mapping changes as 'logically necessary,' failing to distinguish pre-randomization screening from ITT; line 96 turns three-year recruitment into a five-year recruitment window, and line 116 says a research CT with approval ensures scans will not be for research only. Multiple citation markers are unresolved. Overall usable but cannot be considered to have a sufficiently reliable analysis plan.

F.rationale: The exploratory value is preserved, but lines 36/46 write PA, language, and reading as seven times when it is actually only three, exaggerating the data density of the most important analyses. Line 54 directly judges that a d=.67 effect is consistent and power is sufficient based on 28% individual improvement, which cannot be derived without variance information; line 9 further says low power can be offset by 'precise effect estimation.' Line 62 broadly treats MNAR without imputation as reasonable, overlooking bias. The supporting conclusion itself is not the problem; the certainty of the supporting basis is too high.

external_checks.finding: The 2022 review reports within-group standardized changes and their intervals, most of which are indeed near zero; this cannot be unconditionally equated with the effects of two new randomized groups.

The reduction of task conditions for children aged eight and under is a protocol choice made for time, attention, and cooperation considerations, not proof that this age group cannot complete all conditions or that there is a floor effect.
The two-arm procedures include program generation; developmental indicators have only three waves; the planned recruitment range totals 56–64, not 72; MNAR resampling does not fix selection bias.
